correctness.rationale: For all real 2^(-1/2)<=c<1, six caps are disjoint up to null sets. Nine linearly independent degree-four harmonic polynomials diagonalize both sphere and cap pairings. Forty-five exact bilinear checks verify all eigenvalue formulas, with sector dimensions 1+2+3+3 and trace 27(1-c). A convex cubic has exactly one root in (7/10,3/4); two strict comparison factorizations and negative Bernstein coefficients exclude competing sectors. This is an analytic all-parameter proof, corroborated by direct quadrature of the full Gram matrix at four radii.

value.rationale: In contrast to exact concentration on the same six-axis region at degree two, where one sector always dominates, the first full four-sector analysis at degree four exhibits a new symmetry-sector phase transition. An exact, natural nine-dimensional multi-cap Slepian invariant for six octahedrally distributed observation regions is fully classified. The first even harmonic degree with all four octahedral symmetry sectors exhibits a unique algebraic switch from a three-dimensional to a one-dimensional optimal mode, with four-dimensional degeneracy at the transition; two tempting competing sectors never maximize. The exact configuration and dimensions, not just a small constant improvement, motivate the invariant.
